source: <app>Parlatype</app> is an easy to use media player. Its main purpose is to help you transcribing speech.
target: <app>Parlatype</app> is an easy to use media player. Its main purpose is to help you transcribing speech.

source: For a quick overview have a look at <link xref="first-steps"/>. Other topics are covered below.
target: For a quick overview have a look at <link xref="first-steps"/>. Other topics are covered below.

source: Drop files, file names or timestamps on Parlatype
target: Drop files, file names or timestamps on Parlatype

source: You can drop files, file names or timestamps on <app>Parlatype</app>’s window.
target: You can drop files, file names or timestamps on <app>Parlatype</app>’s window.

source: Files: Drag and drop a file from a file manager, e.g. <app>Files</app>, on <app>Parlatype</app> and it will open that file.
target: Files: Drag and drop a file from a file manager, e.g. <app>Files</app>, on <app>Parlatype</app> and it will open that file.

source: File names: Select a file name from a word processor, e.g. <app>LibreOffice</app>, drop the selected text on <app>Parlatype</app> and it will open that file. This will always work if the selection contains a full path. If you select the name only, <app>Parlatype</app> will look up its full path in the list of recent files and open it if it can find it in that list.
target: File names: Select a file name from a word processor, e.g. <app>LibreOffice</app>, drop the selected text on <app>Parlatype</app> and it will open that file. This will always work if the selection contains a full path. If you select the name only, <app>Parlatype</app> will look up its full path in the list of recent files and open it if it can find it in that list.

source: Timestamps: You can drag and drop timestamps to <app>Parlatype</app>. Select a timestamp from a word processor, e.g. <app>LibreOffice</app>, drop the selected text on <app>Parlatype</app> and it will jump to that position.
target: Timestamps: You can drag and drop timestamps to <app>Parlatype</app>. Select a timestamp from a word processor, e.g. <app>LibreOffice</app>, drop the selected text on <app>Parlatype</app> and it will jump to that position.

source: <app>Parlatype</app> is an easy to use audio player to help you transcribing or annotating recorded speech. You need to run a word processor, e.g. <app>LibreOffice</app>, too. Launch <app>Parlatype</app> and open an audio file by clicking on the <gui>Open</gui> button in the upper left corner.
target: <app>Parlatype</app> is an easy to use audio player to help you transcribing or annotating recorded speech. You need to run a word processor, e.g. <app>LibreOffice</app>, too. Launch <app>Parlatype</app> and open an audio file by clicking on the <gui>Open</gui> button in the upper left corner.

source: You can also drag and drop a file on <app>Parlatype</app>.
target: You can also drag and drop a file on <app>Parlatype</app>.

source: In the lower left corner there are the controls with a <gui>Play</gui> button which toggles between play and pause. Whenever you pause, <app>Parlatype</app> rewinds a few seconds to make it easier to resume. This can be changed in the Preferences dialog.
target: In the lower left corner there are the controls with a <gui>Play</gui> button which toggles between play and pause. Whenever you pause, <app>Parlatype</app> rewinds a few seconds to make it easier to resume. This can be changed in the Preferences dialog.

source: The buttons <gui>Skip backward</gui> and <gui>Skip forward</gui> in the lower left corner skip a few seconds back or ahead. The amount of time can be changed in the Preferences dialog.
target: The buttons <gui>Skip backward</gui> and <gui>Skip forward</gui> in the lower left corner skip a few seconds back or ahead. The amount of time can be changed in the Preferences dialog.

source: The view scrolls automatically so that the cursor is always visible. You can scroll manually by clicking on or dragging the scroll bar or using the standard keybindings. Automatic scrolling is stopped then.
target: The view scrolls automatically so that the cursor is always visible. You can scroll manually by clicking on or dragging the scroll bar or using the standard keybindings. Automatic scrolling is stopped then.

source: To get back to the cursor’s position and let the view scroll automatically again, click on the menu button showing the time and then on <gui>Go to Cursor</gui>. Clicking on the <gui>Play</gui> button also turns automatic scrolling on.
target: To get back to the cursor’s position and let the view scroll automatically again, click on the menu button showing the time and then on <gui>Go to Cursor</gui>. Clicking on the <gui>Play</gui> button also turns automatic scrolling on.

source: Clicking in the view with the right mouse button will put the cursor there. The left mouse button is for <link xref="selections"/>.
target: Clicking in the view with the right mouse button will put the cursor there. The left mouse button is for <link xref="selections"/>.

source: The <gui>speed scale</gui> next to the <gui>Volume</gui> button in the lower right corner lets you adjust the speed of playback. A value of 1 means normal speed, everything lower (down to 0.5) is slower, everything above is faster.
target: The <gui>speed scale</gui> next to the <gui>Volume</gui> button in the lower right corner lets you adjust the speed of playback. A value of 1 means normal speed, everything lower (down to 0.5) is slower, everything above is faster.

source: How to play and repeat a selection
target: How to play and repeat a selection

source: You can select a piece of the waveform with the mouse. Next time you press <gui>Play</gui>, it will play the selection only. When it is finished and you press <gui>Play</gui> again, it will loop the selection once.
target: You can select a piece of the waveform with the mouse. Next time you press <gui>Play</gui>, it will play the selection only. When it is finished and you press <gui>Play</gui> again, it will loop the selection once.

source: When in selection mode, you can not exit the selection anymore until you deselect it.
target: When in selection mode, you can not exit the selection anymore until you deselect it.

source: Selections can be made with the mouse (or pointer device) with a left click, holding the mouse button and dragging the pointer. If you click with <key>Shift</key> key pressed, an already existing selection will be enlarged to that point.
target: Selections can be made with the mouse (or pointer device) with a left click, holding the mouse button and dragging the pointer. If you click with <key>Shift</key> key pressed, an already existing selection will be enlarged to that point.

source: To deselect click once with the left button into the waveform. If the waveform has keyboard focus, you can press <key>Escape</key>.
target: To deselect click once with the left button into the waveform. If the waveform has keyboard focus, you can press <key>Escape</key>.

source: Timestamps help you to navigate in your transcription.
target: Timestamps help you to navigate in your transcription.

source: Timestamps can look like this: #03:45.2#. You can select them with or without the number signs.
target: Timestamps can look like this: #03:45.2#. You can select them with or without the number signs.

source: <app>Parlatype</app> can produce different timestamp formats, they can be set in the Preferences dialog.
target: <app>Parlatype</app> can produce different timestamp formats, they can be set in the Preferences dialog.

source: If you select the timestamp in the word processor, you can drag and drop it on the <app>Parlatype</app> window and it will go to that position. This is also possible the other way round: Drag the time label from <app>Parlatype</app> to a word processor and drop it there to insert it.
target: If you select the timestamp in the word processor, you can drag and drop it on the <app>Parlatype</app> window and it will go to that position. This is also possible the other way round: Drag the time label from <app>Parlatype</app> to a word processor and drop it there to insert it.

source: Clicking on the menu button that is showing the current time you can <gui>Copy Time to Clipboard</gui> or <gui>Go to Time in Clipboard</gui>.
target: Clicking on the menu button that is showing the current time you can <gui>Copy Time to Clipboard</gui> or <gui>Go to Time in Clipboard</gui>.

source: This can also be done with keyboard shortcuts. First make sure, the <app>Parlatype</app> window has focus. With the key sequence <keyseq><key>Ctrl</key><key>c</key></keyseq> the current timestamp is copied to the clipboard. Changing to the word processor you can insert now the timestamp in your transcription.
target: This can also be done with keyboard shortcuts. First make sure, the <app>Parlatype</app> window has focus. With the key sequence <keyseq><key>Ctrl</key><key>c</key></keyseq> the current timestamp is copied to the clipboard. Changing to the word processor you can insert now the timestamp in your transcription.

source: To go to a timestamp position, copy the timestamp in the word processor to the clipboard. Once you have changed focus to <app>Parlatype</app> press <keyseq><key>Ctrl</key><key>v</key></keyseq>.
target: To go to a timestamp position, copy the timestamp in the word processor to the clipboard. Once you have changed focus to <app>Parlatype</app> press <keyseq><key>Ctrl</key><key>v</key></keyseq>.

source: Let Parlatype do part of the transcription work
target: Let Parlatype do part of the transcription work

source: <app>Parlatype</app> offers automatic speech recognition that is done on your computer. No data is sent over the network.
target: <app>Parlatype</app> offers automatic speech recognition that is done on your computer. No data is sent over the network.

source: <app>Parlatype</app> must have been built with <app>PocketSphinx</app>. Please note that those libraries might be not available on your platform.
target: <app>Parlatype</app> must have been built with <app>PocketSphinx</app>. Please note that those libraries might be not available on your platform.

source: <app>Parlatype</app> has no built-in text editor. You need the Parlatype Extension for <app>LibreOffice</app> to output recognized text.
target: <app>Parlatype</app> has no built-in text editor. You need the Parlatype Extension for <app>LibreOffice</app> to output recognized text.

source: Select a language model in the Preferences Dialog, <gui>Speech Recognition</gui> tab, see <link xref="asr-setup"/> for more details.
target: Select a language model in the Preferences Dialog, <gui>Speech Recognition</gui> tab, see <link xref="asr-setup"/> for more details.

source: Open the main menu and click on <gui>Automatic Transcription</gui>. This is only available, if you have setup and chosen a language model.
target: Open the main menu and click on <gui>Automatic Transcription</gui>. This is only available, if you have setup and chosen a language model.

source: Now press <gui>Play</gui> in <app>Parlatype</app> and the recognized speech will be printed in <app>LibreOffice</app>, if the Parlatype Extension is installed. Output is silent because decoding speed is dependent on your machine and may be slower or faster than real-time speech.
target: Now press <gui>Play</gui> in <app>Parlatype</app> and the recognized speech will be printed in <app>LibreOffice</app>, if the Parlatype Extension is installed. Output is silent because decoding speed is dependent on your machine and may be slower or faster than real-time speech.

source: Output is without punctuation or capitalization, you have to add or correct that yourself.
target: Output is without punctuation or capitalization, you have to add or correct that yourself.

source: Accuracy depends on many factors like quality of the recording, background noise, speaker’s dialect or pronunciation and the speech model used. For general transcription you can expect an word error rate between 10 and 50 %. Alas this means that in some cases manual transcription from the start will be faster than automatic transcription and the following correction process.
target: Accuracy depends on many factors like quality of the recording, background noise, speaker’s dialect or pronunciation and the speech model used. For general transcription you can expect an word error rate between 10 and 50 %. Alas this means that in some cases manual transcription from the start will be faster than automatic transcription and the following correction process.

source: For speech recognition you need a language model: one or more files trained with real speech samples. Parlatype supports language models made for CMU Sphinx and ships a couple of language model configurations.
target: For speech recognition you need a language model: one or more files trained with real speech samples. Parlatype supports language models made for CMU Sphinx and ships a couple of language model configurations.

source: A language model configuration contains meta data describing the language model: A name that you can change, the language it was made for, speech recognition engine, publisher, license etc. It has a (third party) link, where you can download the files. Part of the configuration is the base folder, where you have saved the model. Additionally it contains various parameters for the plugin which are not shown.
target: A language model configuration contains meta data describing the language model: A name that you can change, the language it was made for, speech recognition engine, publisher, license etc. It has a (third party) link, where you can download the files. Part of the configuration is the base folder, where you have saved the model. Additionally it contains various parameters for the plugin which are not shown.

source: Open the Preferences Dialog and click on the <gui>Speech Recognition</gui> tab. Initially there are no configurations available, click on the <gui>Copy Initial Set of Configurations</gui> button.
target: Open the Preferences Dialog and click on the <gui>Speech Recognition</gui> tab. Initially there are no configurations available, click on the <gui>Copy Initial Set of Configurations</gui> button.

source: Depending on your installation you will see then a list of downloadable configurations.
target: Depending on your installation you will see then a list of downloadable configurations.

source: Select a configuration by clicking on it. There is a short description of the model and where you can download it. After downloading, you have to set the folder where your download resides. You can also change the <gui>Display name</gui>.
target: Select a configuration by clicking on it. There is a short description of the model and where you can download it. After downloading, you have to set the folder where your download resides. You can also change the <gui>Display name</gui>.

source: An installed model has no label next to it. Select a model and press the <gui>Activate</gui> button to use this model for speech recognition. The active configuration is indicated by a <_:media-1/> symbol.
target: An installed model has no label next to it. Select a model and press the <gui>Activate</gui> button to use this model for speech recognition. The active configuration is indicated by a <_:media-1/> symbol.

source: Shipped configurations might get obsolete over time. Therefore you can import a configuration with the <gui>+</gui> button. Configurations are text files with an .asr ending.
target: Shipped configurations might get obsolete over time. Therefore you can import a configuration with the <gui>+</gui> button. Configurations are text files with an .asr ending.

source: To remove a configuration, select it and click the <gui>Delete</gui> button.
target: To remove a configuration, select it and click the <gui>Delete</gui> button.
